item.title: Did Slow Horse's season finale cliffhanger give us a major James Bond casting clue?
item.description: The sixth season of the hit TV show Slow Horses has come to an end, and with it a cliffhanger that could have major casting implications when it comes to the identity of the next James Bond...

item.title: Meta shares jump 5% as AI investments fuel revenue growth
item.description: Meta Platforms said Wednesday that its third-quarter profit jumped more than threefold, as the social media giant's revenue climbed sharply, adding to confidence that the firm's AI spending is improving the business.

item.title: Moment Colombian authorities seize 7.6 tonnes of cocaine bound for Europe
item.description: Colombia has seized 7.6 tonnes of cocaine at the port of Cartagena in what President Abelardo de la Espriella described as the country's largest drug seizure in a decade.

item.title: 'Everything' in Ukraine is now a target for Putin, says EPP MEP
item.description: EPP MEP Pekka Toveri believes Russia has “taken all the rules off" the table and is increasingly targeting residential areas, as well as cultural and government buildings. He warns that the attacks could leave large parts of Kyiv "uninhabitable" during the winter.

item.title: Public order a 'big failure of the government', says French MEP Jean-Marc Germain
item.description: Public order in France "allows rioters to destroy shops and public buildings," says MEP Jean-Marc Germain. He comments on the recent protests and violence beleaguering France last weekend, calling the scenes witnessed a "big failure of government."

item.title: Serbia: Student protesters flood Belgrade ahead of snap elections
item.description: Cheers, music and waving flags greeted students arriving in Belgrade from across Serbia on Wednesday, as thousands gathered ahead of a final rally before this weekend's snap parliamentary elections.

item.title: French police union to sue government over mishandling of riots
item.description: Stanislas Goudon, a representative from the French national police union Alliance, comments on the recent wave of protests and violence in France from a police perspective, criticising significant government ill-preparedness for the demonstrations.

item.title: Russian strikes kill 7 in Ukraine after US envoy meets Putin
item.description: Ukraine's air force posted a warning in the early hours of "more ballistic missiles towards Kyiv" and instructed residents to stay in shelters.

item.title: One interest rate, three inflation realities. Why Europe’s price shock is so uneven
item.description: Finland, Germany and Lithuania share the euro and the ECB’s 2.50% deposit rate, but with September inflation at 2.7%, 3.3% and 6.1% respectively, they show how one policy meets different price realities.

item.title: A fraught push for peace, and a race to fund Ukraine
item.description: Good morning. It’s Mared Gwyn with your Thursday newsletter. Today: the fraught push to revive peace talks between Ukraine and Russia, cash for Kyiv becomes intertwined in talks on the next EU budget, and Argentina’s Milei reignites a war of words with Spain’s Sánchez.

item.title: Europe Today: France under fire as Macron faces backlash, Putin opens door to Ukraine peace talks
item.description: France prepares for another weekend of protests as Macron faces criticism over his Gulf tour. Meanwhile, Putin signals readiness for Ukraine peace talks after meeting Steve Witkoff, and Hungary detains former central bank governor György Matolcsy over suspected fraud.

item.title: ‘This used to be paradise’: How intensive farming is destroying Europeans’ favourite swimming spots
item.description: 'Green sludge' is appearing on Europe's shorelines as warming waters, sewage and agricultural runoff fuel the growth of toxic algae.

item.title: Tesla's profit drops as it explores a possible merger with Musk's other public company, SpaceX
item.description: Tesla reported a decline in third-quarter profit, but generated more cash than analysts expected, leaving investors with a mixed picture as it explores a possible merger with Elon Musk's other big company, SpaceX.

item.title: Kenichi Yoda, Princess of Asturias laureate: "Ghibli is closely tied to its time"
item.description: The new president of the legendary Japanese studio argues that beauty must be sought even when portraying horrors such as war. In Oviedo, Yoda, Ghibli’s public face, says they will continue to explore contemporary themes and concerns, just as their founders did.

item.title: Drinking tea could lower your risk of stroke, but only if it’s not too hot
item.description: Drinking tea three or more times a week is linked to an 11% lower risk of vascular disease, such as stroke or heart attack, a new study suggests. However, burning hot tea was linked to the opposite effect: a 16% increase in vascular disease risk.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 22nd, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 22nd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Residences, shower spas and private lofts: The most luxurious airline experiences ranked
item.description: Think luxury travel is all about the seat? A new ranking of the ‘most outrageous’ luxury airline experiences has found that not all perks begin at takeoff…

item.title: Marine Le Pen vs Alice Weidel: How the far right wants to reshape the EU
item.description: AfD leader Alice Weidel unveiled her EU vision in Strasbourg a week after Marine Le Pen did the same in Brussels. Both parties seek to reshape the bloc around national sovereignty but differ on fiscal policy, energy and the extent of reform.

item.title: Canada unveils $6.2bn plan to shield manufacturers as Trump trade tariffs bite
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney said the Trump tariffs make both US and Canadian industries weaker and reduce choice for households in both countries.

item.title: El Salvador launches military operation in Haiti to free four kidnapped aviation technicians
item.description: Bukele warned that failure to free the men who have been missing since Sunday’s attack on an armoured vehicle would trigger a far more powerful operation.

item.title: Yemen: Tanks fire as fighting erupts on the outskirts of Taiz
item.description: Tanks and gunfire mark renewed clashes on the outskirts of Taiz. Inside the Yemeni city, mounting rubbish and blocked roads are raising concerns about public health.

item.title: Disappointed after meeting, French unions call for 5 November action
item.description: Trade unions, unanimously disappointed after their meeting with the government, are calling for a large mobilisation on 5 November. The CGT's general secretary is urging workers to "generalise the strike".

item.title: Greece: Thousands flood Athens streets in education protest
item.description: Thousands of protesters marched through Athens on Wednesday 21 October, demanding greater investment in education. Crowds filled the streets of the capital, waving banners, chanting slogans and beating drums as they made their way past the Greek parliament.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV post-op results show no further treatment required as tumour was localised
item.description: The pontiff needs no further treatment, his doctors said, eight days after an hour-and-a-half operation on his right lung.

item.title: Aberfan: King Charles marks Welsh mining disaster that killed a generation of children
item.description: Survivors shared their memories with the royal party, six decades after an official verdict, a raid on donations and a fight over the tips that followed.

item.title: Lithuania seizes major synthetic drugs lab run by Dutch national
item.description: Police recover more than 500kg of methamphetamine and 300kg of amphetamine in a three-day operation targeting a suspected international supply network.

item.title: Colombia seizes 7.6 tonnes of Netherlands-bound cocaine at Cartagena port
item.description: Separately, two Dutch nationals wanted by prosecutors in the Netherlands have been arrested in Colombia.

item.title: Thélyson Orélien row: publisher says AI used to write 'C'était ça ou mourir'
item.description: The Quebec author has been at the centre of a controversy for weeks. On Wednesday, his Canadian publisher Les Éditions du Boréal admitted that AI was indeed used to write his latest novel.

item.title: Riots in France: tourism sector fears drop in foreign visitors
item.description: Images of the riots in France, broadcast worldwide, are already slowing hotel bookings, and tourism professionals fear ongoing violence will further deter foreign visitors.

item.title: Dussehra: Giant effigies of demons go up in flames in India
item.description: India celebrated Dussehra, or Vijayadashmi, in New Delhi with Ravana effigies set ablaze, fireworks and the prime minister joining the festivities.

item.title: EU journalism prize awards investigation into human rights abuse at Italy’s migrant centres in Albania
item.description: An investigation published by Dutch platform De Correspondent on the controversial Italy-Albania migration deal, now seen as a model for deportation hubs outside the EU, has won the Daphne Caruana Galizia Prize.

item.title: Zelenskyy backs freezing front line as first step towards Ukraine ceasefire
item.description: The Ukrainian leader insists Kyiv must have a seat at any negotiations and wants security guarantees from Washington and European allies, as a row over slowed SpaceX satellite services rumbles on.

item.title: Nine Emperor Gods Festival: Devotees walk across burning embers for good luck
item.description: Devotees walked on fire for good luck at Malaysia’s Nine Emperor festival, with fireworks, a lion dance and blessings at a temple in Kuala Pilah.

item.title: Qatar in Motion | Made in Qatar: Local brands with global ambitions
item.description: This episode of Qatar in Motion explores how local talent is driving economic diversification. We reveal how innovation, enterprise and ideas are being proudly made in Qatar and finding its way to the global stage.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 21st, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 21st, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Milei reignites war of words with Sánchez as Spanish PM declares himself ‘leftie and proud’
item.description: Javier Milei has reignited his war of words with Pedro Sánchez during a visit to Madrid, as the Spanish prime minister declared himself “leftie and proud”.

item.title: African health ministers to hold Ebola crisis talks as Nigeria confirms first case
item.description: African health ministers will hold crisis talks on Ebola as Nigeria becomes the fourth country to confirm a case. The patient is now in isolation, while her contacts, including her spouse, a Swiss national, are being monitored.

item.title: EU should revive talks on broader China trade deal, top MEP says
item.description: As EU lawmakers prepare to visit Beijing, the European Parliament's trade chief is calling for a broader agreement that could revive elements of a frozen investment pact and address unfair Chinese trade practices across multiple industries.

item.title: Poland’s abortion reforms would leave it among the EU’s most restrictive, even if signed into law
item.description: Poland’s parliament, Sejm, has voted to ease some of the country’s abortion restrictions, but the changes would leave its laws among the most restrictive in the European Union — and face an uphill battle to become law.

item.title: Roaming roots: Artist Gulnur Mukazhanova explores her nomadic heritage at Frieze London
item.description: Presented in collaboration with Turkish Airlines, artist Gulnur Mukazhanova brought her ongoing Bosağa textile series to Frieze London 2026.

item.title: Brussels goes back to the drawing board on Europe-wide taxes
item.description: European Council President António Costa has taken over the negotiations on the bloc's next long-term budget, with one of the biggest question marks being how he will resolve the challenge of new EU-wide taxes.

item.title: UN warns El Nino could be strongest on record as it urges world to prepare
item.description: The UN's aid chief says the humanitarian system cannot cope alone, as $50 million is released for 11 frontline countries including Chad and Somalia.

item.title: EU prosecutors raid far-right group's offices in €4 million funds scandal
item.description: The searches are linked to an probe into the alleged misuse of more than €4 million by the now-defunct Identity and Democracy group, whose debts Patriots for Europe could be forced to repay.

item.title: Eurozone government debt climbs to 88.8% of GDP as Italy closes in on Greece
item.description: Government debt in the eurozone rose to 88.8% of GDP in the second quarter of 2026, with Italy closing in on Greece, the most indebted member state, and France's debt climbing to 119.1% as its borrowing costs topped 5%.

item.title: Macron calls for extreme caution in Gulf, secures critical gas deal in Qatar state visit
item.description: French president concludes his state visit by reinforcing the strategic partnership with Qatar. He declares his Gulf tour objectives achieved after securing a crucial gas deal with Qatar as he seeks to lower tensions over living costs in France.

item.title: Airbnb bans check-out chores like stripping the bed or taking the bins out
item.description: Hosts can no longer ask guests to do anything that would take “significant effort or time, or would typically be performed by a cleaner”.

item.title: Feeding Our Tomorrow: how India’s women-led, sustainable farming is reaching Europe
item.description: India showcases sustainable, tech-driven farming and women’s empowerment at SIAL Paris 2026, as a new EU-India trade deal reshapes food ties.

item.title: Dialogue in the dark: David Bowie meets Nina Simone at Steve McQueen's exhibition at Guggenheim Bilbao
item.description: Steve McQueen’s exhibition “66–76–26” at Guggenheim Bilbao Museum is a sound sculpture with no image. It is a link between the decades, the emotion of love and understanding, and it also stars David Bowie and Nina Simone.

item.title: This country aims to attract €18B in cleaner energy investment
item.description: Kazakhstan aims to mobilise €18 billion in investment in cleaner energy through its just energy transition platform, QaJET, with support from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).

item.title: Angolan-Portuguese singer IAMDDB accuses Israel of stealing her identity in AI video
item.description: Angolan-Portuguese artist IAMDDB has condemned the unauthorised use of her likeness in an AI-generated propaganda video shared by Israel's official social media accounts. The Manchester-based singer accuses the government of using her image without permission.
